newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends steady on pre-holiday covering.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends steady on pre-holiday covering.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICALS
Sept (3rd pos) 1,153 rgt/tonne July (south) 1,195*
Open/Hi/Low 1,155/1,158/1,144 Prev close 1,195
Prev settlement 1,153 * sellers prices

PALM OIL FUTURES - Ended steady on late short-covering ahead of Thursday's public holiday. Uncertainties of the impact of the U.S. Midwest weather on soy products kept players busy strategising positions, and prompted many to sell for profit.
Latest export, production and stocks data point to a bearish supply and demand situation. Friday range seen at 1,140-1,160.
PALM OIL PHYSICALS - Saw buying by refiners.
"They (the players) were worried about the weather conditions in the U.S., which are changing by the day," said a trader in Kuala Lumpur.
"Both on the long and short, people could get caught and that's why they take profits the moment when they hear the weather's fine and cover when they hear it's not good," added the trader.
Dealers said the market was also clouded by fears of a further build-up in stocks, after the release of latest trade and production data on Tuesday.
Cargo surveyor SGS said that July 1-15 exports were 307,536 tonnes against 290,935 tonnes in the corresponding period in June.
The Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) put official stocks at the end of June at 786,123 tonnes, up from 712,289 tonnes at end-May.
"Basically, if we head in this direction, we're going to have a higher production and stocks situation in the next three months," said another trader.
"Unless we export at least 700,000 tonnes a month over the next three months, which is doubtful, I don't see us averting a glut," added the trader.
Dealers said on a positive note, the weak ringgit against the U.S. dollar has made Malaysian palm oil bought on the greenback cheaper and more competitive than Indonesian.
Towards the close, it was Thursday's holiday that turned the market around, said the dealers.
"People just wanted to be covered for the next two nights that Chicago is going to be opened when we are closed," said one dealer.
The new third-month October futures closed unchanged at 1,153 ringgit ($447.85) a tonne.
The physical market saw continued buying by refiners.
Among physicals, July (south) crude palm oil saw offers at 1,195 ringgit against bids at 1,192.50, after trading between 1,185 and 1,192.50.
July (central) saw offers at 1,180 ringgit versus bids of 1,175, after trading from 1,170 to 1,175.
Aug (south) was offered at 1,195 against bids of 1,192.50, after trading at 1,190 and 1,192.50. Aug (central) saw offers at 1,180 against bids of 1,175, with earlier trade at 1,170 to 1,175.
In refined products, Aug/Sep RBD palm oil was offered at $492.50 a tonne FOB Malaysia, and Oct/Nov/Dec at $490.
Aug RBD palm olein saw offers at $530, Sep at $527.50 and Oct/Nov/Dec at $527.50. Aug was traded at $530 and $527.50.
Aug RBD palm stearin was offered at $372.50 while Aug/Sep palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $290.
-- K. Baranee Krishnaan (603-275-6834) ($1=2.5745 ringgit)
